correctness.rationale: Inspected original source proof. All three generators gcd1; for n≥4 minimal generators. The classical 3-generator symmetry/gluing criterion reduces symmetry to d=gcd(u,v)>1 and remaining z∈<u/d,v/d>. Derived pair gcd bounds (≤30), then if a>d(c−a) the number of generators in a putative gluing must equal d and forces impossible 8n+6|d. The inequality a>30(c−a) is 2n²−241n−180>0 at n≥122, excluding all large n. Independent integer modular-inverse scanning for n=2..121 gave exactly {2,3,6,7,8,18} and explicit gluing certificates. The 24 reduced candidate pairs in source are consistent with this. The n=3 redundant third generator is handled by the two-generator semigroup; quoted Frobenius/genus from gluing formula. The infinite exclusion is analytical, not a finite scan.

value.rationale: Symmetric (equivalently Gorenstein/2g=F+1 in numerical semigroups) is a standard structural invariant. The ordinary hexagonal three-generator family and its Frobenius sequence pre-exist; a sharp infinite classification with late exception n=18 answers a natural nontrivial question not mechanically given by the Frobenius table. The explicit cutoff and six exceptions form a complete motivated classification.
